title: Strengthen generator config and sweep validation
lead: Define and enforce a clear generation-config contract for invalid or impractically large sweep configurations, while preserving fixed, sweep, and max mode behavior that the docs describe.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: Generation config validation checks basic shape, but does not reject duplicate sweep axes or arithmetic overflow in the sweep cardinality. Invalid or excessively large inputs should fail clearly before expensive allocation or output.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body: Obfuscator/Obfuscator.cs; Obfuscator/DataGenerator.cs; Obfuscator.Tests/ObfuscatorTests.cs; generator examples and README.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body: Add cases for duplicate axes, invalid discrete values/config combinations, sweep-cardinality overflow, and supported fixed/sweep/max behavior including seeded output.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: Define validation for sweep axis uniqueness, referenced values, relevant numeric and percentage fields, and checked sweep cardinality before row expansion. Preserve documented row modes and avoid introducing an arbitrary size cap without a documented rationale.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: Run focused config/generator tests, compare the frozen semiconductor fixture, then run the full solution test suite.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Do not regenerate or overwrite the committed golden CSV or suite fixtures as part of unrelated generator tests.
